subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A repeated rhythmic or melodic pattern, common in world and minimalist music, is an:
questions.explain: An ostinato is a persistently repeated musical pattern.

questions.q: 'Legato' means to play notes:
questions.explain: Legato means smooth and connected, with no gaps between notes.

questions.q: What does a 'coda' provide at the end of a composition?
options: A concluding section that rounds off the piece
questions.explain: A coda is a concluding section added to round off and finish a piece of music.

questions.q: Which cadence ends on chord V, sounding unfinished?
questions.explain: An imperfect cadence ends on chord V and sounds incomplete.

questions.q: A major triad is built from which intervals above the root?
questions.explain: A major triad stacks a major 3rd then a minor 3rd, giving a bright sound.

questions.q: Which clef is also known as the G clef and is used for higher-pitched instruments?
questions.explain: The treble (G) clef curls around the G line and is used for higher pitches.

questions.q: Compared with a major scale, a (natural) minor key generally sounds:
questions.explain: Minor keys typically sound darker or sadder than the brighter major.

questions.q: Two quavers together are worth the same as one:
questions.explain: Two quavers equal one crotchet beat.

questions.q: Which note value lasts the longest?
questions.explain: A semibreve lasts four beats in 4/4, longer than a minim, crotchet or quaver.

questions.q: What does MIDI stand for in music technology?
questions.explain: MIDI stands for Musical Instrument Digital Interface, a protocol linking electronic instruments and computers.

questions.q: Which term describes a melody supported by chords moving in the same rhythm?
questions.explain: Homophonic texture is a clear melody accompanied by chords.

questions.q: How many different pitches does a pentatonic scale contain?
questions.explain: A pentatonic scale is made up of five different pitches per octave.

questions.q: Which Italian tempo term means 'fast and lively'?
questions.explain: Allegro means fast and lively, whereas adagio and largo are slow.

questions.q: A 'pedal' (or pedal point) in texture is:
options: A sustained or repeated note, often in the bass, held under changing harmonies
questions.explain: A pedal is a held or repeated note, usually in the bass, that continues while harmonies change above it.

questions.q: 'Quantising' in a DAW is used to:
options: Correct the timing of notes onto the beat
questions.explain: Quantising snaps recorded notes to the nearest beat to tidy up their timing.

questions.q: A texture in which all parts share the melody but decorate it differently at the same time is called:
questions.explain: Heterophonic texture has performers playing variations of the same melody simultaneously.

questions.q: In vocal technique, 'vibrato' is:
options: A slight, regular wavering of pitch to enrich the tone
questions.explain: Vibrato is a slight, regular variation in pitch that adds warmth to a sustained note.

questions.q: On a guitar, a 'capo' is used to:
options: Raise the pitch of all strings to play in a different key
questions.explain: A capo clamps across the fretboard to raise the pitch of every string, changing the key.

questions.q: How many beats does a dotted minim last in 4/4 time?
questions.explain: A dot adds half the note's value, so a minim (2 beats) plus its dot (1 beat) lasts three beats.

questions.q: The articulation marking 'accent' (>) tells a performer to:
options: Hold the note longer than written
questions.explain: An accent mark instructs the player to stress or emphasise that note.

questions.q: The interval from C up to G is a:
questions.explain: C up to G spans five letter names, making a perfect 5th.

questions.q: A DAW used for recording and sequencing music stands for:
questions.explain: DAW means Digital Audio Workstation, software used to record, edit and sequence music.
